results.fact: Line of the 40-50 degree traverse (under the West Peak vs across the East Peak's SW face)
results.evidence: One recent trip report describes bypassing the West (false) summit by dropping into the west basin, reaching a broad saddle, then hugging the steep west ridge of the East Peak and bypassing outcrops on the south slope — which supports parts of BOTH the beta (saddle, west ridge, south-side traverse) and the variant (going around, not over, the West Peak). Another report notes parties either climb to the col between the peaks or take a more direct line. No second source fixes where the 40-50 degree slopes lie or whether the final section above the connecting ridge is short, so the two descriptions may be complementary halves of one line; not patched.

results.fact: Which summit the route climbs (West Peak vs true East Peak)
results.correct_value: The route targets the true East Peak (6,891 ft); the West Peak is the false summit passed on the way.
results.evidence: Itinerary, waypoints, overview, approach, climbing_route, descent_text and high_point_ft all take this route to the East Peak; only beta (a lifted West Peak description), face and pitch_detail[3] name the West Peak. External sources agree the East Peak (6,891 ft) is the higher true summit and that the scramble heads northeast from the trail end toward it.

patches.fact: Which summit the route climbs (West Peak vs true East Peak)

patches.replace: This route continues past the West Peak false summit to the higher East Peak (6,891 ft), the mountain's true summit. The maintained trail ends on the shoulder near 5,400-5,600 ft; everything above is unmaintained boot path and open scrambling.

results.fact: West Peak elevation and trail reach
results.correct_value: Maintained trail ends near 5,400-5,600 ft; above that is ~1,000 ft of unmaintained boot path to the false summit (no trail to within 50 ft of the summit).
results.evidence: The land manager says the maintained trail ends at about 5,400 ft on the shoulder, with a further ~1,500 ft of gain beyond it; a hiking database puts the official end at a 5,600 ft ridge crest with an unofficial path 0.8 mi and 1,000 ft further to the false summit. The beta's 'trail to within 50 ft' sentence is replaced by the patch recorded under the previous fact (same beta sentence), which also drops the disputed 6,721 figure. Note: the West Peak's own top is given as 6,721-6,725 ft by two sources, versus the ~6,600 ft 'false summit' figure used in the rest of the row; whether the false summit is the West Peak top or a lower point is not settled, so those copies were left alone.

results.fact: Two different summit lines (over/around the West Peak to a notch vs down into the basin and up a gully)
results.evidence: Both lines exist: trip reports describe going to the col between the West and East peaks, or a more direct line involving a gully, and summit descriptions mention staying in a gully that becomes exposed near the top. But the notch line's '~1,400 ft' from a col ~300 ft below a ~6,600-6,725 ft false summit to a 6,891 ft summit cannot close (it would be ~500-600 ft); no source gives the col elevation, so the figure was not rewritten.

A route summary gives 10 mi round trip with 5,000 ft gain for the East Peak; a detailed trip guide measured 11.4 mi and 4,793 ft. An out-and-back with a ~300 ft drop and regain must have equal gain and loss; ~5,000 ft fits both sources and the itinerary.

results.fact: Mileage to the trail end and knob
results.evidence: A hiking database puts the 5,200 ft viewpoint knob at mile 2.7 and says the official trail runs another half mile along the crest (implying ~3.2 mi), yet lists 8.2 mi round trip (4.1 mi one way) — internally inconsistent. The land manager gives the trail end at ~5,400 ft with no mileage. No second source pins the mileages, so the approach's 'knob around mile 4' / '~4.1 mi' and the waypoints' 2.9 / 3.4 were not changed.

results.evidence: One reference gives July-September as the most favourable months; a detailed trip guide gives July to October. The row's own climate text says October works only in low-snow years. Sources split, so neither season nor best_season was changed.

Glacier/snowfield remnants lie between the summits and a trip guide says microspikes can help year round on steep heather, but no two sources agree that an ice axe is needed at all times versus early season only. Not patched.

External route summaries rate the scramble Class 2, agreeing with rock_grade, while grade, pitch_detail and required skills say Class 2-3 and describe an exposed knife-edge crux. Downgrading the displayed grade on safety-relevant terrain on the strength of summary ratings (which may describe the West Peak) is not safe to do blind; left open.

Whether a self-issued wilderness registration exists at the trailhead (access.permit / permit vs overnight_permit 'none') was not confirmed by any source and was left as is.
